issues.title: Unqualified perturbed-contraction claim

failure_location.quote: the learned projected operator is contractive on the anchored subspace with a contraction factor of the form

issues.failure_explanation: Under the old assumptions, the proof yields the bound with factor gamma plus C_q,infinity C_infinity,q N epsilon_b. If that quantity is at least one, it is only a Lipschitz bound and does not establish contraction. The formal appendix accordingly assumes gammahat<1, whereas the main lemma asserted contraction under the projection-deviation conditions alone.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma overstates stability for learned gauges with insufficiently small estimation error. Later SA results are not affected by this omission because they separately assume gammahat<1 or choose M to enforce it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the perturbation bound with its explicit factor, for example \(\widehat\gamma=\gamma+C_{{\rm q},\infty}C_{\infty,{\rm q}}N\varepsilon_b\), and call the learned operator contractive only under the additional condition \(\widehat\gamma<1\) (equivalently, for sufficiently small \(\varepsilon_b\)).
issues.why_classification: The proof establishes a Lipschitz factor but does not establish contraction unless that factor is below one, so this is not a transcriptional typo. The missing small-perturbation qualification is nevertheless a short, routine, source-supported repair that preserves the bound and intended contraction regime; no listed downstream result is affected because later SA results separately impose or enforce \(\widehat\gamma<1\).

issues.title: SA rate omits the uniform noise-moment hypothesis

failure_location.quote: Assume the structural learning and weight estimation steps succeed and assume $\widehat\gamma<1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem claims the O(T^{-1/2}) rate after assuming only successful structural and weight learning and gammahat<1. Its proof chain controls the projected martingale term by a fixed sigma squared through eq:oracleB and eq:step3_noise_bound. Those stated assumptions do not provide such a uniform conditional bound; the oracle noise depends on the current iterate. Thus the proof invokes an unestablished premise. The closing reference to constants depending on a bound does not supply its existence or uniform conditional form.
issues.overall_effect: The main SA rate, and hence its main-text end-to-end corollary, is established only for oracles satisfying the additional uniform conditional second-moment condition, not under all conditions stated in v1. The detailed appendix results that explicitly assume eq:oracleB remain valid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to the hypotheses of the main SA-rate theorem a uniform conditional second-moment bound on the oracle noise along the iterates, with respect to the algorithmic filtration, and carry that hypothesis into the end-to-end corollary. Leave the stated \(O(T^{-1/2})+O(N\varepsilon_b)\) rate unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The proof genuinely invokes an unstated premise, so the theorem is unreliable as written and the defect is not a typo. However, the required moment condition is explicit in the detailed appendix theorem and is already anticipated by the main theorem's dependence on an oracle second-moment bound. Adding this standard local SA hypothesis repairs both the theorem and its corollary without changing the algorithm, conclusion, convergence rate, or intended bounded-noise regime.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Assume the structural learning and weight estimation steps succeed, the oracle noise has a uniform conditional second moment bound, and $\widehat\gamma<1$.

issues.title: Wrong absorption-time symbol in the query bound
issues.failure_explanation: Each of the |T| M_abs absorption episodes costs an expected number of transitions bounded by the scalar H_abs. The old display instead uses H, which is introduced at eq:Lyap_series as a d-by-d Lyapunov matrix. Consequently the asserted query count is ill-typed; the main-text corollary already shows the intended H_abs factor.
issues.overall_effect: Only the explicit appendix query-count expression is malformed; the sample-budget orders and the correctly written main-text query bound are unchanged.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the matrix symbol \(H\) in the appendix query-count expression by the scalar expected absorption-time bound \(H_{\mathrm{abs}}\), yielding \(nK_{\mathrm{graph}}+|\mathcal T|M_{\mathrm{abs}}H_{\mathrm{abs}}+nT\).
issues.why_classification: The old source uniquely forces this correction: \(H\) is defined as a Lyapunov matrix and cannot multiply episode counts to form a scalar query budget, whereas \(H_{\mathrm{abs}}\) is the defined scalar absorption-time bound and already appears in the corresponding main-text count. No mathematical inference or guarantee needs repair.
